performance.suspectCount: {count, plural, one {# suspect value} other {# suspect values}} (> 100% or negative dropout), excluded from ranking and equity
performance.methodCoverage: Cumulative coverage over the period = day-weighted mean of the annualized monthly rates (Σ numerators ÷ Σ denominators, constant annual target). WHO IA2030 thresholds: target 90%, critical below 80%. A value > 100% points to an underestimated denominator.
performance.methodDropout: Cumulative dropout over the period = (Σ Penta1 doses − Σ Penta3 doses) ÷ Σ Penta1 doses. Target ≤ 5%, critical above 10%. A negative value points to a reporting inconsistency.
performance.zonesSuspect: {count, plural, one {# suspect zone} other {# suspect zones}} (excluded)
performance.topZones: Provinces with the most zones below threshold
performance.topLost: Provinces with the most children to catch up
performance.noZoneData: Health-zone data unavailable for this period.
performance.noZoneBelow: No health zone beyond the critical threshold ({threshold}%).
performance.zonesNote: Each province is coloured by the share of its health zones in the critical band for {indicator} ({unit}{threshold}%, WHO IA2030 per-district bound): green = none, orange ≤ 10%, red > 10%. Suspect zones (> 100% or negative dropout) are excluded.
performance.lostNote: Children who received Penta1 but not Penta3 over the period (Σ Penta1 doses − Σ Penta3 doses). An absolute number, independent of the target population: reliable even where coverage exceeds 100%.

wastage.pendingSync: Doses used per antigen are being synced (SIGL ESS): the per-antigen wastage rate will appear after the next ETL run. The overall rate and doses administered are already available.
wastage.method: Source: SIGL ESS 2025. Wastage rate = (doses used − doses administered) ÷ doses used, as in the DHIS2 "LMIS … (Taux de perte)" indicators; the overall rate applies the same formula to all vaccines. Thresholds depend on the presentation (WHO indicative rates): critical above the indicative maximum (1 dose 5%, 2–5 doses 10%, 10–20 doses reusable after opening 25%, 10-dose lyophilised 40%, 20-dose lyophilised 50%), target at about half. A negative rate (more doses administered than used) points to a reporting inconsistency.

supply.sourceNote: Source: SIGL ESS 2025. % facilities in stock-out = facilities reporting at least one stock-out day of the antigen in the month ÷ facilities managing that antigen (AMC or stock-out days reported). Thresholds: target ≤ 5%, critical above 10%.

help.faq1a: SIVAX is the decision-support platform for the immunization sector in the DRC. It brings vaccination, stock, cold chain and surveillance indicators together in one place, as dashboards, maps, alerts and reports.
help.faq2a: Everyone involved in the programme: decision-makers get an overview and the key points of concern, analysts can explore details by province and health zone, and partners can receive reports tailored to their needs.
help.faq3q: Where does the data come from, and is it up to date?
help.faq3a: It comes from the national health information system (SNIS RDC's DHIS2), the ministry's official source. It is updated automatically twice a week. The current month only appears once health facilities have finished reporting, to avoid misleading figures.
help.faq4a: Yes. Access requires a personal account, and each user only sees what their role allows. Connections are encrypted, sensitive settings are stored encrypted, and inactive sessions close automatically. SIVAX only holds aggregated data: no individual patient data.
help.faq5a: Yes. SIVAX works on phones, tablets and computers. You can also install it as an app: from your browser, choose "Install" or "Add to Home Screen".
help.faq6q: Do I need technical skills to use it?
help.faq6a: No. Dashboards are readable at a glance, with colour codes (within standard, to watch, critical). To go further, the AI assistant answers questions asked in plain language, typed or spoken.
help.faq7q: Can I trust the AI assistant's answers?
help.faq7a: The assistant relies only on the platform's official data and never makes up figures: if data is missing, it says so. It helps interpret results, but decisions remain your teams'; always check an important figure in the corresponding dashboard.
